g.text: 4. How the per-state table of a device is filled

g.data-qualified-name: Configurators .ticked by the PRG before the device.
g.text: Configurators (ticked by the PRG before the device)

g.data-qualified-name: Configurators .ticked by the PRG before the device..FB_CC_StatePMPSConfig
Configurators .ticked by the PRG before the device..FB_CC_StatePMPSEncConfig
Configurators .ticked by the PRG before the device..FB_CC_StateDefaultsConfig
Configurators .ticked by the PRG before the device..FB_CC_InternalStateConfig

g.text: Each configurator is bound inline to one ST_PositionState
slot. The PRG sets the position, the PMPS key and a stDefault
baseline. It sits in the PRG, not in the device, because a
declaration initialiser cannot index a reference that is nil
The device layers its own per-state name and fDelta defaults
on top of what the PRG set. Variants: PMPSEnc adds the encoder
count, Defaults only sets the baseline without a PMPS key.
